title: bug: pre-freeze-pinned-documents times out at random on a 5s budget, redding the root lane for every row
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 20:35-20:50 local at HEAD c2f726d3 by worker-bcaa6d5e from the epic-final row task-99f364e3, while running root `pnpm test` as a DoD-1 leg.

THE FAILURE, verbatim:
  FAIL packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts > pinned corpus authority (task-e1b47913) > refuses a corpus that moves between the two authority observations
  Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  at packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts:158:3

IT IS A FLAKE, NOT A DEFECT IN ANY DIFF, and it is measured as one rather than asserted. Four full root runs in one hour: RED, GREEN, GREEN, RED. Then the file STANDALONE, three consecutive runs with nothing else on the host: `Tests 1 failed | 11 passed (12)`, then `12 passed (12)`, then `12 passed (12)`. Same bytes, same HEAD, different answer — roughly one failure in three either way, so root file-parallelism is not the cause and neither is any concurrent suite.

THE SHAPE. The arm builds real git corpora on disk (`newCorpusRepo`) and is bounded by vitest's DEFAULT 5000 ms test timeout — no explicit budget on the `it`. Spawning git and writing a corpus twice is not reliably a sub-5-second operation on this host, so the arm races its own default. Its ELEVEN siblings in the same file pass every time; only the arm that observes a corpus TWICE is affected, which is consistent with a duration problem rather than a logic one.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ROW: root `pnpm test` is a DoD-1 leg for many rows on this board, including every integration row. A one-in-three red that belongs to nobody's diff burns a full-suite run — about three minutes plus a gate lease — every time it fires, and it teaches readers to discount root reds, which is how a real one gets missed.

ATTRIBUTION: nothing in task-99f364e3's owned paths is involved. That row's files are `tests/e2e/foundation/platform-{pipeline,pipeline-harness,teardown-failure-paths,secret-canary}` and `docs/agent-stack-runbook.md`; the failing file is `packages/benchmark/src/`, and it fails standalone with those files present but not executing.

DEFINITION OF DONE
1. The arm's budget matches the work it actually does, or the work is made cheap enough for the default — a retry or an exclusion is NOT acceptable and neither is raising the global `testTimeout`.
2. Evidence it is fixed rather than made rarer: at least TEN consecutive standalone runs green, count lines quoted. One green run proves nothing against a one-in-three flake.
3. The other eleven arms in the file keep their current behaviour and budgets.
4. Root `pnpm test` EXIT 0 with its count line quoted.
definitionOfDone: The timing-out arm is bounded by a budget that matches the git-corpus work it performs, or that work is made cheap enough for the default: not a retry, not an exclusion, and not a raised global testTimeout.

At least TEN consecutive standalone runs of packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts are green with count lines quoted, because one green run cannot distinguish a fix from a one-in-three flake.
The other eleven arms in the file keep their current behaviour and budgets.
Root pnpm test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE ARM'S ACTUAL DURATION BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. NO EDITS. DoD 1 says the budget must match "the work it actually does" — that is a number you read, not one you pick.

Run the file standalone with per-test durations printed:
  npx vitest run packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts --reporter=verbose
Measured at plan time on an IDLE host, and re-measure rather than trusting these:
- "refuses a corpus that moves between the two authority observations" — **2317ms against the default 5000ms budget**. That is 46% of its budget consumed with nothing else running. A 2.2x slowdown under fleet load reds it, and the filing measured roughly one failure in three, which is exactly what a 2.2x margin on a loaded host looks like.
- "never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority" — **1721ms**. See step 4: it is the next one to flake and it is NOT this row's to fix.
- "a repository holding uncommitted content" — 698ms. Everything else is under 65ms.
- File total 5.01s, tests 4.83s.

NOW ACCOUNT FOR WHERE THE 2317ms GOES, because the filing names only half of it. The arm at :158 does FOUR expensive things, not two:
1. `newCorpusRepo("moving", false)` at :159 — mkdtemp plus THREE git spawns (`init`, `add`, `commit`), and process spawn is expensive on win32.
2. `readPinnedCorpusAuthority()` at :161 — the production read, which spawns git again.
3. `vi.resetModules()` + `vi.doMock("node:fs")` + `await import("./pre-freeze-pinned-documents.js")` at :163-174 — the module graph is re-transformed and re-evaluated under a mock. NO OTHER ARM IN THIS FILE COMBINES A CORPUS BUILD WITH A MODULE RE-IMPORT; :194 builds a corpus without re-importing and :204 re-imports without a corpus. That combination is the discriminator, and it is why only this arm flakes.
4. `fresh.readPinnedBenchmarkSpec()` — two more authority observations, each spawning git.

AND READ THE MOCK AT :165-172 CLOSELY, because it is the finding the filing missed: `readFileSync` is replaced by a function that calls `real.writeFileSync(join(root, "landed-mid-read.md"), …)` on EVERY invocation — including every file the module loader reads during the `await import` on the next line. The arm needs the tree to move ONCE, between the two authority observations. Count how many times that write actually fires (a counter in a scratch run, not a committed change). If it is more than a handful, that is unbudgeted disk work inside a 5-second window and it is step 2's target.

Record all durations and the write count in the step note.

THREE BASELINE RUNS, `npx vitest run packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts --reporter=verbose`, host currently far quieter than at plan time. All 12/12 green:

FINDING 1 — THE ARM'S DURATION IS ~100% HOST LOAD, NOT WORK. Same bytes, same commit: 340ms here, 2317ms at plan time, >5000ms in the filing. That is a ~15x spread on ONE host. Nothing about the arm changed between those observations, so any budget must be sized for the loaded tail, not for the number I can measure.

FINDING 2 — THE PLAN'S STEP-2 PREMISE IS FALSE, MEASURED. Instrumented the mock with a counter and surfaced it via a deliberate `expect(__writes).toBe(-1)` (console.log is swallowed in this repo's vitest runs): `AssertionError: expected 1 to be -1`. The mock's `real.writeFileSync` fires EXACTLY ONCE, on exactly the corpus read the arm's comment (:152-157) intends. It does NOT fire on module-loader reads during `await import` — vitest's loader does not route its own file reads through the `vi.doMock("node:fs")` factory, and neither `pre-freeze-audit-vocabulary` nor `pre-freeze-source-reader` calls `readFileSync` at load. There is no unbudgeted disk work to remove; narrowing the mock will remove 0 writes and ~0ms. Step 2's own text anticipates this ("If it did not move materially, say so plainly"), so this is recorded, not blocked.

FINDING 3 — WHERE THE TIME ACTUALLY GOES. Phase timers inside the arm, surfaced the same way, on a 693ms run:
  `repo=164 auth=385 import=5 read=135 writes=1`
- `newCorpusRepo("moving", false)` = 164ms (3 git spawns)
- `readPinnedCorpusAuthority()` at :161 = 385ms (2 git spawns; `git status --porcelain=v2 -z --untracked-files=all` is the single most expensive call in the arm)
- `vi.resetModules()` + `vi.doMock` + `await import` = **5ms**
- `fresh.readPinnedBenchmarkSpec()` = 135ms (4 git spawns: before rev-parse+status, after rev-parse+status, plus the file read and the one mock write)
git-attributable: 684ms of 693ms = **98.7%**. Module re-import is **0.7%**. So the plan's second cheapening theory ("the module graph is re-transformed and re-evaluated under a mock") is also measured near-zero. NINE git subprocess spawns are the entire cost.

CONSEQUENCE FOR STEPS 2-3. The only remaining cost lever is `newCorpusRepo` (:41-53) and the production authority reads. DoD 3 forbids touching the shared helper (also used by the :92 sweep case and :194), and the production reads are the subject under test. So the explicit per-arm budget in step 3 carries the WHOLE fix; step 2 will still narrow the mock to a path gate because it makes the code match its stated intent and hardens it against a future dependency reading files at load, but I will not claim a speedup it cannot produce.

Confirmed the repo idiom for step 3 exists: `}, 30_000);` at packages/benchmark/src/freeze-manifest-admission.test.ts:390, packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-discovery.test.ts:144, packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-current-hold.test.ts:538, plus three under tests/integration/.

implementationPlan.description:
MAKE THE WORK CHEAP BEFORE MAKING THE BUDGET BIG (DoD 1's first branch).

DoD 1 offers two routes and they are not equally good. Raising a number hides the cost; removing the cost is a fix. Do this one first, then size the budget in step 3 against the reduced work.

NARROW THE `node:fs` MOCK at :165-172 so the tree moves ONCE, at the moment the arm's comment says it should. That comment (:152-157) states the intent precisely: "it is a property of the corpus DURING the read — the fs read is wrapped only to supply that timing". A mock that writes on every `readFileSync` in the process is broader than that intent, and the extra writes land during module loading rather than during the observation the arm is about. Fire the write on the corpus read only — gate it on the path being read, or on a one-shot latch, whichever expresses the intent more plainly in the code.

THIS MUST NOT WEAKEN THE ARM. It still has to observe the corpus TWICE with a real move in between, and still has to reach the same refusal from the same layer. If narrowing the mock makes the move miss the window, the arm stops testing its subject — which is worse than a flake. Step 4's drill exists to prove the arm still fails when the production refusal is removed.

DO NOT TOUCH `newCorpusRepo` (:41-53). It is shared with the sweep cases and with the arm at :194, and DoD 3 says the other eleven arms keep their current behaviour. Making the shared helper cheaper would change theirs too. If you believe the three git spawns should become fewer, say so for a follow-up rather than doing it here.

Re-measure with `--reporter=verbose` and record the arm's new duration beside the 2317ms baseline. If it did not move materially, say so plainly — then the budget in step 3 carries the whole fix and the record should show that honestly rather than implying a speedup that did not happen.

GIVE THE ARM AN EXPLICIT BUDGET SIZED FROM THE MEASUREMENT (DoD 1's second branch).

Add an explicit per-`it` timeout to the arm at :158 — the third argument, the idiom already used elsewhere in this repo (`}, 30_000);`). Size it from step 2's re-measured duration with headroom for a LOADED host, not for the idle one you measured on: this board runs up to seven seats, and the flake only appears when git spawns are competing. A multiple in the region of ten times the observed duration is the right order; state the number you chose AND the measurement it came from in a comment on that line, so the next person can re-derive it instead of guessing whether it was arbitrary.

WHAT DoD 1 FORBIDS, and each for a real reason:
- NOT a retry. A retry turns a timing bug into a slower timing bug and destroys the evidence that anything was wrong.
- NOT an exclusion. The arm covers a condition no static corpus can pose (its comment at :152-157); excluding it retires the coverage.
- NOT a raised GLOBAL `testTimeout`. That would hand every arm in the repo a bigger budget to hide in, including ones whose slowness is a real defect. The budget belongs on the arm that earns it.

DO NOT ADD A BUDGET TO ANY OTHER ARM IN THIS FILE. DoD 3 says the other eleven keep their current budgets, and the sibling at :186 (1721ms) is explicitly out of scope here — see step 4.

ARCHITECT architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 — PLANNED (4 steps / 1 file). I RAN THE FILE at plan time; the numbers confirm the filing's diagnosis and add two things it did not have.

**MEASURED, idle host, all 12 green** — `npx vitest run packages/benchmark/src/pre-freeze-pinned-documents.test.ts --reporter=verbose`:
```
refuses a corpus that moves between the two authority observations   2317ms   <-- the flake
never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority 1721ms   <-- the NEXT flake
refuses at its own code when a repository holding uncommitted content 698ms
everything else                                                      <=65ms
File total 5.01s (tests 4.83s)
```
The failing arm consumes **46% of its 5000ms default with nothing else on the host**. The filing measured roughly one failure in three; a 2.2x margin on a seven-seat board is exactly what that looks like. The diagnosis is confirmed, not merely plausible.

**WHERE THE 2317ms GOES — FOUR COSTS, and the filing names two.** (1) `newCorpusRepo` at :159 — mkdtemp plus THREE git spawns (`init`, `add`, `commit`), expensive on win32. (2) `readPinnedCorpusAuthority()` at :161 — spawns git again. (3) `vi.resetModules()` + `vi.doMock("node:fs")` + `await import(…)` at :163-174 — the module graph re-transformed and re-evaluated under a mock. (4) `fresh.readPinnedBenchmarkSpec()` — two more authority observations, each spawning git.

**THE DISCRIMINATOR, which explains why only this arm flakes**: no other arm in the file combines a corpus build with a module re-import. `:194` builds a corpus without re-importing; `:204` re-imports without a corpus. Only `:158` does both. That is a duration explanation and it matches the filing's own point that the logic is not at fault.

**THE FINDING THE FILING MISSED, and the reason the plan does not just raise a number.** The mock at :165-172 replaces `readFileSync` with a function that calls `real.writeFileSync(join(root, "landed-mid-read.md"), …)` on EVERY invocation — including every file the module loader reads during the `await import` on the very next line. The arm needs the tree to move ONCE, between the two authority observations. As written it moves on every read in the process while the mock is installed: unbudgeted disk work inside a 5-second window. The arm's own comment at :152-157 states the narrower intent — "the fs read is wrapped only to supply that timing". Step 2 narrows the mock to that intent, which REMOVES cost rather than hiding it; step 3 then sizes an explicit per-arm budget against the re-measured duration. DoD 1 says "or", so either alone would satisfy it — doing the cheapening first means the budget absorbs real work rather than waste.

**NOT TOUCHED, deliberately**: `newCorpusRepo` at :41-53 is the largest single cost and the obvious target, but it is shared with the sweep's DIRTY_REPO case (:92) and with :194. DoD 3 says the other eleven arms keep their current behaviour, so making the helper cheaper is out of scope. Named as a follow-up rather than done quietly.

**EVIDENCE BAR RAISED ABOVE DoD 2's LETTER.** Ten green runs alone cannot distinguish "fixed" from "quiet host" — ten greens at 4900ms would satisfy DoD 2 while the flake sits one loaded host away. Step 4 requires the arm's DURATION be quoted for each of the ten runs with min/max/median, so the margin between observed max and the new budget carries the argument. And the caveat gets stated rather than papered over: the worker does not control host load.

**TWO DRILLS, because a bigger budget makes a broken arm green as easily as a slow one.** (i) Remove the production refusal and require the arm to go RED **on its assertion, not on a timeout** — that is the guard against narrowing the mock so far the tree stops moving inside the observation window, which would retire the coverage and is strictly worse than the flake. (ii) Set the budget below the measured duration and require the timeout to return, proving the budget is load-bearing.

**HANDED ON, NOT FIXED HERE — the next flake is already measured.** The sibling at :186, "never lets a caller-supplied SHA stand in for observed Git authority", runs **1721ms against the same 5000ms default** — a 2.9x margin, same corpus helper, no explicit budget. DoD 3 forbids changing its budget in this row. Step 4 requires the worker to file it as a follow-up or record it here with the measured duration. Leaving it unmentioned is how this row gets re-filed in a fortnight under a different arm's name.

These ten ran on a host whose load I do not control, and it was quiet: the same arm measured 2317ms at plan time and >5000ms in the filing, on the same bytes. So the run COUNT settles almost nothing here — ten greens at 4900ms would have satisfied DoD 2's letter while the flake sat one loaded host away. git-attributable: 684 of 693ms = **98.7%**. NINE git subprocess spawns are the entire cost. THE GATE WAS KEPT ANYWAY, for a correctness reason rather than a speed one: ungated, the FIRST readFileSync in the process moves the tree. Today that is the corpus read. A dependency that later reads a file at module load would move the tree BEFORE the first authority observation, both observations would then see the same dirty tree, and the arm would refuse at CORPUS_ROOT_DIRTY — a different code, retiring the moved-tree coverage while still looking green.
